candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles and appropriate precautions based on client condition and transmission risk.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — burn care and isolation precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply Standard Precautions to burn care and add pathogen- or syndrome-specific Transmission-Based Precautions when indicated rather than assigning a universal isolation category solely because of the burn injury.

options.A: Apply Standard Precautions to every patient and add Transmission-Based Precautions when an infectious agent or clinical syndrome warrants them; burn injury alone does not create one universal special isolation category.
options.B: Place every patient with a major burn in Airborne Precautions solely because loss of the skin barrier creates airborne transmission risk.
options.C: Use no gloves or gowns for burn wound care unless a culture has already identified a multidrug-resistant organism.
options.D: Use a Protective Environment room for every burn patient because this CDC category was designed for all patients with impaired skin barriers.

candidate.rationale: CDC isolation guidance uses two tiers: Standard Precautions for all patients and Transmission-Based Precautions for patients with known or suspected infectious agents requiring additional measures. CDC also notes that special precautions for burn patients as a universal category are an unresolved issue rather than a blanket isolation recommendation. Protective Environment guidance is specifically directed to allogeneic HSCT patients, not all burn patients. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Burn injury alone does not mandate one universal CDC isolation category; Standard Precautions apply to all patients, with Transmission-Based Precautions added according to suspected or confirmed infection.
candidate.source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions: Preventing Transmission of Infectious Agents in Healthcare Settings
candidate.source_locator: Precautions to Prevent Transmission: Standard Precautions apply to all patients; Transmission-Based Precautions supplement them for specific suspected/confirmed pathogens.
